scope: Primary-source audit of the parameter dependence hidden by f(parameters). An explicit bound may retain absolute big-O constants. A composition involving an unspecified dimensional control function is recorded as a partial expansion, not as a closed formula in the parameters displayed in the atlas.

entries.formulaPlain: O(Δ Σ_{i=1}^{K} (2i−1)(Δ−1)^{i−1}) for Δ ≥ 2, where K = ceil(1/ε); constant for Δ ≤ 1
entries.explanation: Section 6 runs stages i=1,...,K. Stage i removes augmenting paths of length h=2i−1 using at most t_i=Δ(Δ−1)^{i−1} invocations. Each invocation consists of flooding, proposals, and augmentation along paths of length h, and therefore costs O(h) rounds. Summing gives this explicit parameter dependence. The paper does not state an exact integer total. For Δ≤1, taking all edges gives an exact matching after at most one round; this avoids a 0^0 convention in the displayed sum. The supplied proper two-colouring is essential.

evidence.title: Local algorithms in (weakly) coloured graphs
evidence.location: Section 6, augmenting-path algorithm and t_i bound immediately before Theorem 9

entries.formulaPlain: At most 4 rounds (derived phase upper bound, independent of Δ)
entries.explanation: The supplied weak two-colouring permits the Section 4 star-forest construction in an absolute constant number of rounds. The four-round schedule below computes exactly its final star centres without communicating the final edge orientations. Every black vertex with white children becomes a centre. An original white root remains a centre exactly when at least one of its black children has no white children. A white vertex that proposed to a black vertex is a leaf. In the all-depth-two case a root chooses one child for edge reversal, but the choice does not affect the set of centres, so the dominating-set output needs no extra round. This is an implementation upper bound derived from the paper, not a printed exact runtime or a claim of round optimality. Δ occurs in the approximation guarantee, not in the communication radius. The catalogue’s f(Δ) classification can be strengthened to constant.

phases.action: Exchange the supplied weak-colouring bits with all neighbours.
Each black vertex proposes to a white neighbour, its parent in the initial forest.
Each white vertex that received no black proposal proposes to a black neighbour.
Each black vertex tells its white parent whether it received any white proposals. Vertices can now decide whether they are final star centres.

entries.formulaPlain: C(g, ε); no closed dependence on g and ε is stated
entries.explanation: Corollary 4.3 states a parameter-dependent constant C(ε,g). Meta-Theorem I gives a transparent composition of the base algorithm, a dimensional control function, and an error-component diameter bound, but this does not compute a closed function of g and ε. In particular the runtime of the planar (11+ε)-approximation and the control-function constants are not expanded here.

partialExpansion.formulaPlain: T + δ + 2, where T = F(2u+2ρ) + max{u+ρ, b}
partialExpansion.parameters: F is the target class's dimensional control function; u is the base algorithm's uniformity radius; ρ is the problem's verification radius; b is the base algorithm's round complexity; δ bounds weak diameters of the error components. The source uses k and r for u and b; these are renamed to avoid collision with distance/local-radius parameters.

entries.formulaPlain: C(d, g, r), for a fixed dimensional control function
entries.explanation: Theorem 8 gives a class-dependent constant and applies Proposition 2 to Theorem 7. Proposition 3 does give a precise generic composition, but the dimensional control function and the genus base runtime are not reduced to closed expressions in the displayed parameters. The local-genus row therefore has no computed full formula to substitute for f(d,g,r).

partialExpansion.formulaPlain: T + δ + 2, where T = F(2u+2) + max{u+1, b}
partialExpansion.parameters: F is the dimensional control function, u the base algorithm's uniformity radius, b its round complexity, and δ the error-component weak-diameter bound. This is Proposition 3's generic formula, not an explicit formula in d,g,r for Theorem 8.

evidence.title: Approximation Algorithms for Dominating Set on Locally Nice Graph Classes

entries.explanation: The original paper states Oₜ(1), while the thesis explicitly analyzes the same Algorithm 5 in O(t) rounds. It chooses the class control function F_t(r)=(5r+18)t; the remaining residual-diameter term is linear in t. The printed composition is 3 max{F_t(5)+2,F_t(11)+5}+g(t)+3, with g linear. This is an asymptotic bound, not a fully specified exact round count.

entries.formulaPlain: C(g); the proof gives a bound in terms of a dimensional control function
entries.explanation: Theorem 3.2 states C(g). Algorithm 2 inspects radius F_g(10)+5, and Claim 3.3 bounds the residual two-hop components' weak diameters by less than 2(F_g(10)+6)g. Gathering the necessary bounded-radius views and applying the constant-round planar algorithm therefore gives the partial asymptotic expansion below. The proof does not compute F_g(10) as a closed function of g; do not label this an elementary explicit dependence on g or an exact integer runtime.

No complete g,k formula is calculated in this passage.
